title: Erdős Problem #761: Dichromatic Number and Chromatic Number
description: Must a graph with large chromatic number have large dichromatic number? Must a graph with large cochromatic number contain a subgraph with large dichromatic number? The dichromatic number is the minimum k such that every orientation admits an acyclic k-coloring. Status: OPEN.

sections.title: Problem Overview
sections.summary: Imports from `Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph` for graph structure and coloring, plus `Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic` for finite vertex sets.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines `Orientation G` (directed edge assignment), `colorClassEdge` (directed edge relation within a color class), `IsAcyclicColoring` (no monochromatic directed **cycle** via `Relation.TransGen` — the correct mathematical definition from Neumann-Lara 1982), `HasAcyclicColoring`, `dichromNumber` $\delta(G)$, `IsCochromatic` (each class is clique or independent set), and `cochromNumber` $\zeta(G)$.

sections.title: Bridge Lemma
sections.summary: The key `isAcyclicColoring_of_no_mono_edge` theorem: if no directed edge is monochromatic (the stronger condition), then no directed cycle is monochromatic (the acyclic condition). This bridges proper-coloring arguments to the cycle-free definition.

sections.title: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Establishes $\delta(G) \le |V|$ (injective colorings are acyclic), $\zeta(G) \le |V|$ (proper colorings are cochromatic), and the bipartite bound $\delta(G) \le 2$ for 2-colorable graphs.

sections.title: Main Conjectures (OPEN)
sections.summary: States the two open questions as axioms: **Question 1** (Erdős-Neumann-Lara): $\forall k,\, \exists f(k)$ such that $\chi(G) \ge f(k) \Rightarrow \delta(G) \ge k$. **Question 2** (Erdős-Gimbel): $\forall k,\, \exists g(k)$ such that $\zeta(G) \ge g(k) \Rightarrow \exists H \subseteq G$ with $\delta(H) \ge k$.

sections.title: Known Cases and Structural Results
sections.summary: Includes the odd cycle placeholder, subgraph monotonicity $H \subseteq G \Rightarrow \delta(H) \le \delta(G)$ (fully proved), arbitrary orientation construction, and the theorem that proper colorings are acyclic for any orientation.

overview.historicalContext: Victor Neumann-Lara introduced the dichromatic number in his 1982 paper 'The dichromatic number of a digraph', defining δ(G) as the minimum k such that every orientation of G admits an acyclic k-coloring. Erdős and Neumann-Lara then posed the fundamental question: must large chromatic number force large dichromatic number? In 1993, Erdős and Gimbel strengthened this by introducing the cochromatic number ζ(G) — the minimum partition into cliques and independent sets — and asking whether large ζ(G) forces a subgraph with large δ. The problems connect orientation theory with classical coloring: while δ(G) ≤ χ(G) is immediate (proper colorings are acyclic), the reverse direction remains mysterious. Neumann-Lara showed δ(K_n) = ⌊n/2⌋ + 1, far below χ(K_n) = n, demonstrating that dichromatic number can be much smaller. Mohar (2016) proved δ(G) ≤ χ_f(G) (fractional chromatic number), providing a tighter upper bound. The question has deep connections to Ramsey theory and the Burr-Erdős conjecture on oriented graphs.
overview.problemStatement: Must a graph with large chromatic number have large dichromatic number? Must large cochromatic number force a subgraph with large dichromatic number?
overview.text: Must a graph with large chromatic number have large dichromatic number? Must a graph with large cochromatic number contain a subgraph with large dichromatic number? The dichromatic number is the minimum k such that every orientation admits an acyclic k-coloring. Status: OPEN.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines orientations, acyclic colorings (using the correct cycle-free definition via Relation.TransGen), and the dichromatic/cochromatic numbers using SimpleGraph from Mathlib. Both open questions are stated as axioms. The bridge lemma isAcyclicColoring_of_no_mono_edge connects proper-coloring arguments to the cycle-free definition, enabling clean proofs of all structural results.
keyInsights: The **dichromatic number** $\delta(G)$ measures worst-case acyclic coloring across all orientations: $\delta(G) = \min\{k : \forall O,\, \exists$ acyclic $k$-coloring of $O\}$

**Acyclic coloring** means no monochromatic directed **cycle** (NOT the stronger 'no monochromatic directed edge'). These are genuinely different: for $K_3$ with a directed 3-cycle, 2 colors avoid monochromatic cycles but not all monochromatic edges
The inequality $\delta(G) \le \chi(G)$ is immediate since proper colorings have no monochromatic edges, hence no monochromatic cycles
**Cochromatic coloring** relaxes proper coloring by allowing cliques as color classes; $\zeta(G) \le \chi(G)$ since independent sets are trivially cochromatic classes
**Question 2 implies Question 1** via the chain: large $\chi(G) \Rightarrow$ large $\zeta(G) \Rightarrow \exists H \subseteq G$ with large $\delta(H) \Rightarrow$ large $\delta(G)$ by monotonicity

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #761 remains OPEN. Both questions about the relationship between dichromatic number and chromatic/cochromatic number are unresolved. The formalization uses the mathematically correct cycle-free definition of acyclic coloring (Neumann-Lara 1982) and captures the key definitions, open conjectures, and structural results including subgraph monotonicity.
conclusion.implications: Resolving these questions would clarify the fundamental relationship between undirected coloring complexity and directed acyclicity constraints, connecting structural graph theory with orientation problems and Ramsey theory.
openQuestions: Is there a function f such that χ(G) ≥ f(k) implies δ(G) ≥ k? (Erdős-Neumann-Lara conjecture)
Can triangle-free graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number have bounded dichromatic number?
What is the exact dichromatic number of Kneser graphs K(n,k)?
Does the Burr-Erdős conjecture for oriented Ramsey numbers follow from a positive answer to Question 1?
